html:
SMTO-SCH-0007 — The schedule's repeat settings don't fit together

GUID: 1ea1539c-c568-4ed8-9bdc-c88bbf4bdf73
Slug: schedule-recurrence-invalid
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • Some of the repeat options for this schedule contradict each other or are missing, such as a weekly repeat with no days picked or an end date before the start. The schedule wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the schedule editor and look at Repeat. For Weekly, select at least one weekday. A weekly schedule with no days chosen never has a day to run.
  2. Check Ends: if you chose On date, make sure that date is on or after the Starts date; if you chose After, enter how many times it should run. An end before the start, or a missing count, leaves the repeat with no valid runs.
  3. For Monthly or Yearly, check Pattern: fill in Day for Day of month, or The and Weekday for Relative weekday. For Yearly, also pick the Month. SMTO needs to know exactly which day of the month or year to use.
  4. Make sure the Prompt or reminder text isn't empty. SMTO won't save a schedule that has nothing to do or say.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and the Schedules page shows the next run on the day you expect.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and describe the repeat you were trying to set up. Don't keep saving the same settings unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Schedule validation rejected a calendar recurrence or action: missing or incompatible pattern fields (weekdays, day_of_month, week_index/weekday, month, start_date), an inconsistent end range, recurrence combined with interval or next_run_at, or empty action text.

What this means

  • Recurrence validation finds incompatible/missing pattern/range fields, or event creation/update lacks required prompt/notification content or a coherent calendar representation. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Recurrence validation finds incompatible/missing pattern/range fields, or event creation/update lacks required prompt/notification content or a coherent calendar representation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact frequency/range/component or content field rather than changing every timing value.

How to fix it

  • Correct the field named in the message: weekly needs weekdays (0=Monday to 6=Sunday), absolute monthly/yearly need day_of_month, relative patterns need week_index and weekday, yearly needs month, non-default series need start_date, end_date must be on or after start_date, numbered ranges need number_of_occurrences only, calendar recurrence cannot be combined with interval/next_run_at, and the prompt or reminder text must not be empty.
  • Correct the named recurrence or required action-content field, then inspect the next occurrence preview.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported recurrence and action pass validation and their next occurrence preview matches intent.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
